name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,325

entries.clue: Caught geek returning before hot soak (6)

indicatorNotes.returning: something returning goes back the way it came, so C and NERD are read right to left
indicatorNotes.before: placed in front of, so the turned chunk comes ahead of H

blocks.note: c = caught, the cricket scorecard abbreviation
h = hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A nerd, caught out, is sent back to cool off in a hot bath.
annotation.walkthrough: The turnaround covers both 'Caught' and 'geek' together, not just the geek, so the C ends up at the back.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: both mean to wet something right through.

entries.clue: On reflection, grass accepting policemen’s crucial point (7)

indicatorNotes.On reflection: a reflection in a mirror runs backwards, so REED is read right to left
indicatorNotes.accepting: to accept is to take in, so the turned grass takes CID inside it

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
CID = Criminal Investigation Department, the British plain-clothes detectives

annotation.surface: Someone thinks hard about an informer who has gone to the police at a key moment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grass' in the surface is an informer, which suits 'policemen'; here it is the plant.
annotation.definitionFit: In sport the game or point that settles a tied contest is called by this name, so it is the crucial one.

entries.clue: Flyer is upset about losing coat (5)

indicatorNotes.losing coat: a coat is the outside layer, so the first and last letters are shed

blocks.note: someone who regrets something is upset about it; its outer R and S are the coat

annotation.surface: A pilot is annoyed at having left a jacket behind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a pilot or a leaflet; here it is a bird. The phrase 'is upset about' must first become one verb, REGRETS, before anything can be stripped.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: this white heron is a bird, and any bird is a flyer.

entries.clue: Vendor can get supply for part of London (6,6)

indicatorNotes.supply: read as the adverb of supple, 'in a supple way', so the letters bend into a new order

annotation.surface: A stallholder can find stock to sell in a certain part of London.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like the noun, stock for a vendor; it is the adverb from supple. The vendor fits the scene, since the district was long home to London's fruit and vegetable market.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the answer is a district of central London, around the old market and the Royal Opera House.

entries.clue: Capital controls often reversed in part (4)

indicatorNotes.reversed: turned the other way, so the letters are read backwards
indicatorNotes.in part: only a part of the phrase supplies the letters

blocks.note: the letters sit across the word gap, contrOLS Often, and run right to left

annotation.surface: Financial controls are often undone in some measure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' in the surface sounds like money, which 'controls' supports; it is a capital city.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the answer is the capital city of Norway.

entries.clue: Second pop group reduced the rest period (7)

indicatorNotes.reduced: made smaller, so THE is cut short by its last letter

annotation.surface: A second-rate pop group cuts back before a break.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' sits after 'group', as if the band shrank; it works on the following 'the'.
annotation.definitionFit: A religious sense: the weekly holy day on which work stops is a period of rest.

entries.clue: Junior member of parliament currently allowed to ignore note (5)

indicatorNotes.to ignore: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the note is dropped

blocks.note: currently = NOW, with the N taken out
n = note, the letter dropped from NOW

annotation.surface: A junior MP is at present permitted to skip a memo.
annotation.walkthrough: A parliament is the collective noun for owls, so its junior member is a young owl, not a backbencher.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on a collective noun: owls gather in a parliament, and a young owl is its junior member.

entries.clue: Opposed to books penned by ChatGPT? (4)

indicatorNotes.penned by: something penned is shut in, as in a pen, so NT sits within AI

blocks.note: NT = New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
ChatGPT is an example of AI; the question mark flags the example

annotation.surface: Someone is against books written by a chatbot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Penned' reads as written, which suits a chatbot writing books; its job is to enclose.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym used as a preposition: 'anti the plan' means opposed to it.

entries.clue: Start to feel anger about foul ingredient in perfume (12)

indicatorNotes.about: loosely read as 'with regard to', setting the anger alongside the foul part rather than truly around it

annotation.surface: Someone grows annoyed by a bad smell in their scent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Foul ingredient' reads as one phrase, but foul belongs to the wordplay. The setter's 'about' does not wrap anything here; the pieces simply run in order.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this aromatic tree resin has long been used in perfumes.

entries.clue: Two vehicles protecting a third (7)

annotation.definitionNote: read as 'a third vehicle', after the two in the wordplay

indicatorNotes.protecting: guards surround what they protect, so the two vehicles close round A

blocks.note: the letter A, kept between them

annotation.surface: Two vehicles escort a third one in a convoy.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: after two vehicles, 'a third' means a third vehicle.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by context: a towed holiday home is a vehicle, the third after car and van.

entries.clue: Dissenter left after brewing beer (5)

indicatorNotes.after: coming later, so L follows the reworked beer
indicatorNotes.brewing: beer that is brewing is still being worked, so its letters are not yet settled in order

annotation.surface: A protester walked out once the beer was being brewed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like 'went away'; it is just the abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one who refuses to accept authority dissents from it.

entries.clue: Detective barely mentions imprisonment (9)

indicatorNotes.barely: bare means stripped, so MENTIONS is stripped of its outer letters

blocks.note: Det = detective, as in Det Insp
MENTIONS without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A detective only just brings up the subject of jail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Barely' reads as 'hardly'; it means stripped bare.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: being held in custody is a form of imprisonment.

entries.clue: Court following American law (3)

indicatorNotes.following: coming behind, so CT comes after A

blocks.note: Ct = court, as in street names

annotation.surface: A court applies an American law.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the court's abbreviation after the American one, although the clue names the court first.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal sense: a statute passed by a legislature is a law.

entries.clue: Fail to deliver free green energy (6)

indicatorNotes.free: letters set free are loose to settle in any order

annotation.surface: A promise of free green energy is not kept.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a broken political pledge, which is exactly the answer's meaning.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: going back on a promise is failing to deliver on it.

entries.clue: Wandering off on acid across motorway (7)

indicatorNotes.off: food that is off has gone bad, so the letters of ON ACID are spoiled into a new order
indicatorNotes.across: lying across something, so the rearranged letters stretch over M and enclose it

blocks.note: M = motorway, as in the M1

annotation.surface: Someone high on LSD wanders across a motorway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wandering off' looks like one phrase; 'off' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a people who roam from place to place lead a wandering life.

entries.clue: Some rubbish options for clergyman (6)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters of the phrase are used

annotation.surface: The choices offered to a vicar are all poor.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between the two words, which is where hidden answers most often sit.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: this senior church figure is one kind of clergyman.

entries.clue: Heading off, notice teacher and drug user (7)

indicatorNotes.Heading off: the head, or first letter, is taken off

blocks.note: notice = SPOT, minus its first letter

annotation.surface: On the way out, you spot a teacher who takes drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' reads as leaving; it cuts the head off the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang term: a habitual cannabis smoker is a drug user.

entries.clue: Finally realised the setter’s not very bright (3)

indicatorNotes.Finally: at the end, so only the final letter is taken

blocks.note: the setter is I, so the setter's = I'M

annotation.surface: The setter owns up at last to being slow on the uptake.
annotation.walkthrough: The self-mockery is the joke: the setter confesses to being slow-witted.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a double edge: said of a lamp or of a slow-witted person.

entries.clue: First appearance of French bachelor, extremely upset (5)

indicatorNotes.extremely: at the extremes, so only the first and last letters are used

annotation.surface: A French bachelor makes his first public appearance, very distressed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of French' has to be split from 'First appearance' so it means the French word for of.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowing from French: a performer's first public outing.

entries.clue: Unwilling cult aren’t converted (9)

indicatorNotes.converted: something converted is changed into another form, so the letters rearrange

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters; the apostrophe is ignored

annotation.surface: The members of a cult are resisting being converted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Converted' fits a cult's recruiting, which hides its job as an anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone holding back from doing something is unwilling.

entries.clue: Be porky, eating veal primarily (4)

indicatorNotes.eating: what eats takes something inside itself, so LIE swallows V
indicatorNotes.primarily: in the first place, so only the first letter of veal is used

blocks.note: porky pie = lie in British rhyming slang, often cut to 'porky'

annotation.surface: Someone becomes fat from eating mostly veal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Porky' looks like the adjective 'fat', but it is British rhyming slang: porky pie = lie.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to exist, as in 'to be or not to be'.

entries.clue: Range popular once more (5)

blocks.note: an Aga is a British brand of range cooker

annotation.surface: A kitchen stove is in fashion once more.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Range' suggests an extent or mountains; it is a kitchen range, and an Aga is the classic heavy cast-iron one in British country kitchens.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain adverb synonym: doing something a second time is doing it once more.

entries.clue: Move brief economic statement (5)

indicatorNotes.brief: something brief is cut short, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: the government's annual economic statement; its final T is the letter cut

annotation.surface: A finance minister is urged to make a short statement and get moving.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like it describes the statement's length; it trims the last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym, usually in the negative: 'it won't budge' means it won't move.

entries.clue: Struggle to bring in new label for high-quality wine (7)

indicatorNotes.to bring in: to bring something in is to take it inside, so VIE holds N and TAG

blocks.note: to vie is to compete or struggle

annotation.surface: A winemaker has trouble designing a new label for a fine wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Struggle' reads as the winemaker's trouble, but it is the verb that opens up to take the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A wine-trade term: wine from a single good year, prized for its quality.

entries.clue: Moment Republican abandons con (4)

indicatorNotes.abandons: to abandon is to leave, so R walks out of the word it was in

blocks.note: R = Republican, the letter that leaves

annotation.surface: A Republican walks away from a swindle at the critical moment.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer as a moment is chiefly British, from the tick of a clock.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: 'back in a tick' means back in a moment.

entries.clue: Academic representative knocked back aperitif (6)

indicatorNotes.knocked back: something knocked back is sent backwards, so DON REP is read right to left

blocks.note: a don is a university teacher

annotation.surface: A university lecturer and a sales rep down a pre-dinner drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' is drinking slang, apt for a drink, but here it means turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this French anise spirit is often drunk before a meal.
